surveys.summary: 13 template files in lib/email/templates/*.ts split cleanly into two groups by recipient+copy, verified at every call site. SCHOOL-branded (7): enrollment-confirmed, invitation, joined-school, certificate-issued, course-removed, payment-instructions, daily-digest/streak-nudge — recipient is always a student/member, copy speaks as the school, footer prints only schoolName. PLATFORM-branded (6): access-cutoff-warning, downgrade-blocked, payment-failed, payment-request-expired, plan-downgraded, renewal-reminder — recipient is always tenant admin emails (via getTenantAdminEmails or an explicit role='admin' query), footer is the literal string 'LMS Platform Billing' in every one, and colors encode urgency (#dc2626 red / #d97706 amber / #7c3aed violet) which must NOT be swapped for school branding — the platform is speaking to the school here, not the school to its members. Every school-branded call site already has tenantId in scope (some via getCurrentTenantId() in a request context, some as an explicit param in a webhook/cron with no headers) and already fetches tenants.name for schoolName, but NONE of them use tenant_settings.site_name (the override app/[locale]/layout.tsx applies for the UI) nor logo_url nor the theme kit — every school email renders with the platform's hardcoded #2563eb blue regardless of the school's theme. All inline hex found; see files[]. The theme-kit engine (lib/themes/kit.ts) already produces email-safe hex for --brand/--primary/--brand-text (deriveMode always returns these as #RRGGBB via mixOklch/toHex or the brand's own hex), but --primary-foreground (button ink) is ALWAYS one of the two oklch() literals KIT_LIGHT_INK ('oklch(0.99 0 0)' ≈ #fcfcfc) / KIT_DARK_INK ('oklch(0.2 0.02 262)' ≈ #11161f) — never hex — so a brand helper must run it through lib/color/contrast.ts's parseColor()+toHex() before it can go in an email. No web fonts can load in email; KIT_TYPE_PAIRINGS' font names (Lora, Outfit, Instrument Sans, etc.) need a hand-written generic-fallback stack. Recommend deriving the button from deriveKitVars(theme.theme, theme.brand).light unconditionally (even for the Kódigo dark theme, whose `.light` KIT_SURFACES set is exactly the light-mode surface defined for this purpose) so every email body stays on a white/near-white background regardless of the school's default UI mode. No unit tests cover template rendering/branding (only course-removed's locale+escaping is tested). No local email preview path exists for Mailgun sends — sendEmail() silently no-ops (returns false) when MAILGUN_API_KEY/MAILGUN_DOMAIN are unset, which is the default local state; supabase/config.toml's [inbucket] block is Supabase Auth's own mailer (magic links/OTP), a completely separate pipeline lib/email never touches.

risks: buttonInk MUST go through parseColor()+toHex() — if a future edit inlines light['--primary-foreground'] directly into an email's style attribute, every branded button silently renders 'oklch(0.99 0 0)' as a literal (invalid) CSS value in every mail client that doesn't fall back gracefully, which is most of them; this is the single easiest correctness bug to introduce here.

tenant_settings row can be missing even when a theme is set (parseStoredKitTheme/resolveSchoolTheme both tolerate malformed/missing jsonb and fall through to null → platform palette) — the helper must not throw on absent rows, only on genuine DB errors; mirror the existing .maybeSingle()/?? patterns used throughout the codebase.

logo_url stored on tenant_settings or tenants can be a relative path or require a signed URL in some flows — verify the URL is publicly fetchable (no auth) before using it in an tag, since Mailgun/recipient mail clients cannot attach auth headers.

course-removed.ts is a bulk send (all enrolled students in Promise.all) — adding a per-recipient brand lookup is fine since brand is per-tenant not per-student, but the helper must be called ONCE per course-deletion event and reused across all sendEmail() calls, not once per student (avoid N redundant DB round trips).

daily-digest.ts's cron already loops many tenants sequentially; getEmailBrand() adds 2 extra queries (tenant_settings, custom_branding check) per tenant per run — cheap, but should be called once per tenant per sweep and reused for both dailyDigestEmailTemplate and streakNudgeEmailTemplate calls in that tenant's batch, not re-fetched per user.

judgment_calls.question: Should the brand helper require a 'custom_branding' plan check (mirroring layout.tsx), or should every plan's recommended swatch just flow through automatically since resolveSchoolTheme() already gates the brand hex server-side?
options: A) Call hasPlanFeature(tenantId,'custom_branding') inside getEmailBrand() and pass it into resolveSchoolTheme() exactly like layout.tsx does — one extra query per call but zero risk of drift if the gating rule ever changes.

B) Skip the plan check in the email helper — resolveSchoolTheme() already downgrades a non-swatch brand to the theme's recommended swatch when customBranding is false, so a caller passing the STORED (unchecked) value would leak a custom hex to a school without the plan; unsafe.
judgment_calls.recommendation: A — always compute customBranding via hasPlanFeature inside the helper. Same call layout.tsx already makes and is cheap; skipping it (B) is a plan-enforcement bypass.

judgment_calls.question: daily-digest.ts's <h2> currently renders in default black (no explicit color), unlike the other 6 school templates' #2563eb heading. Should brand-coloring daily-digest also color its heading, or only its CTA button (matching current visual behavior)?
options: A) Color only the CTA button (ctaButton() at lines 70-76) with brand.buttonBg/buttonInk, leave the <h2> uncolored as today — minimal diff, matches existing (already-inconsistent) behavior.
B) Also color the <h2> with brand.brandText for consistency with every other school template — changes today's visual output for an existing, already-shipped email.
judgment_calls.recommendation: A for a #765-scoped fix (smallest, lowest-risk diff); flag B as a natural follow-up cleanup once the shared helper exists, since the inconsistency predates #765 and isn't its stated goal.

judgment_calls.question: certificate-issued.ts has two buttons: primary 'Download Certificate' (#2563eb/#fff) and secondary 'Verify Online' (#f3f4f6/#1a1a1a, already neutral). Should the secondary button also pick up any brand color, or stay neutral?
options: A) Leave the secondary button neutral (#f3f4f6/#1a1a1a) — a deliberate visual hierarchy choice (primary vs. secondary action); a school's brand color at low lightness could fail AA on a light background without going through the same derivation kit.ts uses for a filled button.
B) Use brand.brand at low opacity or brand.brandText on a tint background for the secondary button too, for full brand immersion.
judgment_calls.recommendation: A — only re-color the primary CTA. Reusing kit.ts's own hierarchy (primary=brand-filled, secondary=neutral) keeps AA guarantees without inventing a new derived tint for email-only use.

judgment_calls.question: What email-safe font stack should headingFontStack use per KIT_TYPE_PAIRINGS, since none of Lora/Outfit/Instrument Sans/Public Sans/Figtree/Noto Sans are installed on end-user devices and email clients strip @font-face/<link> almost universally?
options: A) Map every pairing except 'classic' (Lora/serif) to the same generic sans stack ('Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif) — 3 of 4 pairings collapse to identical output, only the serif pairing looks visually distinct in email.

B) Try to preserve more nuance by mapping 'friendly' (Outfit/Figtree, rounded/geometric) to a different generic (e.g. 'Trebuchet MS', sans-serif) which vaguely echoes a geometric sans in a few more mail clients.
C) Skip heading-font branding entirely for v1 — only ship color+logo, leave font-family:sans-serif as-is everywhere.
judgment_calls.recommendation: A for v1 (simple, predictable, matches what the fonts actually degrade to on the large majority of mail clients); C is also reasonable if the team wants to ship colors+logo first and defer font branding to a follow-up, since font differentiation in email is inherently low-fidelity.

judgment_calls.question: Should the platform-fallback brand hex (#2563eb) used when a tenant has no theme row match the CURRENT hardcoded email blue (#2563eb, preserves existing appearance) or the actual platform default theme color (teal-cyan oklch(0.52 0.105 223.128) per CLAUDE.md)?
options: A) Keep #2563eb as the no-theme fallback — zero visual change for the large majority of tenants that haven't picked a kit theme yet; purely an email-implementation detail unrelated to #765's actual scope (schools WITH a theme).
B) Derive the fallback from app/globals.css's actual default CSS vars so platform-default and email-default match exactly.
judgment_calls.recommendation: A — out of scope for #765 and lower risk; B is a separate, pre-existing inconsistency (platform UI is teal, transactional emails are blue) that predates this issue and would be its own small follow-up if the team wants pixel-parity.

judgment_calls.question: How should a QA person locally SEE a rendered email, given Mailgun requires real credentials and there's no local catcher for lib/email (only Supabase Auth's Inbucket, which is unrelated)?
options: A) Write a small script (e.g. scripts/render-email-templates.ts) that imports every templates/*.ts function with representative fixture data, writes each {subject, html} to a local .html file, and optionally screenshots each with Playwright (already a project dependency) for a visual gallery/diff.

B) Point MAILGUN_API_URL at a local SMTP-catcher-compatible shim (e.g. Mailhog/Mailpit plus a Mailgun-compatible proxy) — heavier setup, and Mailgun's HTTP API (not SMTP) has no official local emulator.
C) Add a dev-only API route (e.g. /api/dev/email-preview?template=enrollment-confirmed) that renders a template's HTML directly in the browser for quick iteration, gated to non-production.
judgment_calls.recommendation: A (a standalone render-to-HTML-files script, optionally piped through Playwright for screenshots) is the lowest-effort, most reliable option — needs no live Mailgun account, no SMTP emulation, and produces artifacts (HTML + PNGs) easy to diff or attach to a PR. C is a reasonable complement for fast iteration during development but shouldn't replace A as the CI/QA artifact.

surveys.area: Certificates (PDF, HTML view, verify page, badge, preview, template editor) — issue #765
surveys.summary: Every certificate surface hardcodes colors and generic serif fonts; none reads the tenant's theme kit. There are THREE different 'default' color pairs live in the codebase today (blue #3B82F6/#1E40AF as the stored design_settings default, dark-green #1a5632/#0f2b1a as the PDF/HTML fallback when no template exists at all, and #1a73e8/#0d47a1 as the badge fallback), plus a fourth (#2563eb) in the certificate-issued email, and a fifth (purple #a78bfa/#7c3aed) hardcoded into the OG share card for /verify. None derive from lib/themes/kit.ts. The PDF (@react-pdf/renderer 4.9.0) only ever uses the built-in Helvetica family — there is no Font.register call anywhere in pdf-generator.tsx despite a `fontFamily` field existing on DesignConfig that is silently unused. lib/certificates/badge-generator.ts imports `registerFont` from `canvas` but never calls it, so the PNG badge renders in whatever the container's default 'Arial' resolves to. The HTML certificate view (lib/certificate-generator.ts) pulls 'Cormorant Garamond' + 'DM Sans' from Google Fonts CDN links — also hardcoded, not the kit pairing. Good news: lib/color/contrast.ts already converts every OKLCH kit token to real hex via toHex()/mixOklch()/readableButton(), so `deriveKitVars(theme, brand).light['--brand']` and `['--primary']` are already plain `#RRGGBB` strings — no new OKLCH→hex conversion work is needed to get a school's brand color into an email, PDF, canvas or ImageResponse. The distinguishing 'is this template still on the default design' signal already exists and is authoritative: `hasCustomCertificateDesign()` in lib/certificates/default-design.ts, currently used only by the save action to gate the `custom` plan tier — it is not consulted anywhere at render time. Feasibility for kit heading fonts in the PDF is good: @react-pdf/renderer 4.9.0 ships @react-pdf/font backed by fontkit ^2.0.2, which DOES support WOFF2 (confirmed by grepping fontkit's source for WOFF2Font.js/WOFF2Directory.js), contradicting the older 'react-pdf only does TTF' assumption — so a kit heading font (Instrument Sans, Lora, Outfit, Noto Sans) can likely be Font.register'd straight from a Google Fonts CSS2 WOFF2 URL server-side. No @fontsource packages are installed and next/font's downloaded files live inside .next build output as WOFF2 with hashed names, not a stable path to read from — so the practical registration source is a Google Fonts URL fetched at render time (needs a documented fallback to Helvetica/Times on fetch failure), not a bundled local file. The PDF is generated in TWO places that can disagree: once at issue time (issue-certificate.ts step 11, stored to Storage bucket 'certificates' at pdfs/{id}.pdf, URL cached in certificates.pdf_url) and again on-demand, regenerated fresh from current template design_settings, every time someone hits GET /api/certificates/[id]?format=pdf — so a template's design change is reflected immediately in the on-demand PDF but NOT in the already-uploaded pdf_url the verify page links to preferentially. Not every certificate even goes through the PDF/badge pipeline: app/api/certificates/generate/route.ts is a second, lighter issuance path (issueCertificate() local function) that inserts a `certificates` row with no PDF/badge generation at all and no template lookup gate — pdf_url stays null, and the verify/view routes fall back to generateCertificateHTML on the fly, which is where the dark-green #1a5632 fallback actually fires (it only fires when `certificate_templates` is null, which is common on this path).

surveys.summary: app/api/og/route.tsx is a pure text-in/image-out generator: it reads only URL query params (type/site/title/subtitle/badge or the certificate fields), has zero tenant awareness, and paints every card with the same hardcoded purple gradient (#0e0a1c→#1e1038 generic, #120b24→#241245 certificate) regardless of which school is sharing. Runtime is Node.js by default (no `export const runtime` override), which is good news — createAdminClient() and hasPlanFeature() work fine there. proxy.ts DOES run for /api/og (its matcher only excludes _next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico, /monitoring, api/op/, and static image extensions) and sets x-tenant-id from the Host header before intl/auth logic even runs (proxy.ts:264-269), so a crawler hitting the absolute image URL on a school's own subdomain gets the correct tenant resolved automatically — no slug/query param is needed for tenant identity, and none should be trusted for it. Three callers exist: lib/seo.ts's ogImageUrl()/buildPageMetadata() (used by the root layout, courses/[id], products/[productId], and p/[slug] pages) and a bespoke call in verify/[code]/page.tsx for certificates. Critically, courses/[id]/page.tsx passes `image: course.thumbnail_url || undefined` to buildPageMetadata, so /api/og is only used as the course's OG image when the course has NO thumbnail — most courses will bypass the branded card entirely and share their raw thumbnail_url instead, with no brand color/logo overlay at all. The theme-kit engine's own derived button ink (`readableButton().ink`) is frequently an OKLCH string literal (KIT_LIGHT_INK/KIT_DARK_INK = 'oklch(0.99 0 0)'/'oklch(0.2 0.02 262)'), which next/og's satori renderer likely cannot parse — but `--brand` itself is always literal #RRGGBB (BRAND_HEX-validated) and `mixOklch()`/`readableOn()`/`toHex()` in lib/color/contrast.ts already return real `#rrggbb` hex, so the fix is to build the card's colors from those hex-returning helpers directly rather than from deriveKitVars()'s CSS-var map. Logo comes from a free-text URL input (components/admin/branding-settings-form.tsx logo_url — no upload widget, no format/content-type validation, `accept="image/*"` isn't even enforced there), which is both a satori-compatibility risk (SVG support in @vercel/og/satori is unreliable for anything but simple shapes) and a server-side-fetch (SSRF-adjacent) risk once ImageResponse fetches it at request time instead of the browser doing so. Heading-font fidelity (KIT_TYPE_PAIRINGS) would require fetching the actual TTF/OTF bytes from Google Fonts at request time (next/font/google only ships WOFF2, and satori cannot use `--font-heading` CSS vars) — no TTF/OTF assets exist anywhere in the repo today, so that's genuinely new plumbing, not a config flip.
